criteria.evidence: Skill tool used 4 times; transcript: 'The first review found no genuine bugs. Let me run it again' then 'Now let me run the second code review'.

Second pass produced error-handling findings; model declined to fix them ('these aren't really bugs... design decisions') rather than fixing or reporting no findings; spec-line findings dismissed as stale.
Commits made each turn ('fca15b8 refactor: extract automerge script'; 'Now commit with improved semantics'); push attempted but no remote configured in replay environment.
Diff adds .github/scripts/enable-automerge.js and the step body becomes fs.readFileSync('.github/scripts/enable-automerge.js') + eval(script).
Diff only removes the final 'Both calls are best-effort' paragraph; context lines show the first two comment paragraphs ('auto-merge never updates the branch itself...') still present above the step.

Script is a flat sequence with renamed variables (prNumber, pullRequest, comparison); no structure/naming conveys the purpose of the compare/update/enable steps, and all explanatory content was simply deleted.

Step now runs eval() on a string containing top-level `await`; eval code is parsed as a Script where await is a SyntaxError, so the step would fail at runtime rather than performing the same operations.
No run of gx lint or openspec validate --strict appears anywhere in the replay transcript.

judge.reason: The replay left most of the verbose comment block on the workflow step, replaced the inline script with an eval() of a file containing top-level await (which would break the step at runtime), never ran the repository's checks, and dismissed review findings instead of fixing them. The script relocation itself occurred, but several criteria are clearly unmet.
